_comment: The judgment half of the repository map: what each part is FOR, the files
that flow through the pipeline at runtime, the cross-language hops, and the
rules that cut across modules. None of this can be parsed out of the source,
so it is written by hand here and merged on top of the derived facts by
Edit this file, then run `python tools/repo_map.py update`. Never edit
docs/repo-map.json or docs/repo-map.md directly — both are generated.

tracker/manifest.py.role: The _manifest.xlsx schema and every read/write of it. Owns RequestItem, Status, Override, load_manifest(), write_statuses() (lock-retry, then a pending-JSON sidecar merged on the next write) and create_template().
tracker/manifest.py.notes: Every other module goes through this to touch the manifest. create_template() writes ONLY the accountant's columns — scanner state is written separately by write_statuses(), which is why seeding a test fixture takes both calls. Workbook saves go through save_workbook_atomically() (write beside, os.replace) so a crash mid-save never leaves a manifest Excel cannot open. identifier_problem() refuses identifiers that could not survive as a folder-name prefix (illegal characters, trailing dot); duplicates are compared case-insensitively because Windows folders are.

tracker/scaffold.py.role: Turns a manifest into folders: Shared/ (the client's one drop folder) + Shared/PBC/, and Prepared/{Identifier} - {Document}/ plus 00 - Needs Review. Writes the client's _README.txt.
tracker/scaffold.py.notes: Also the home of the path constants every other module imports: MANIFEST_FILENAME, SHARED_DIR_NAME, PBC_DIR_NAME, PREPARED_DIR_NAME, REVIEW_DIR_NAME.

tracker/validators.py.role: Tiers 1-2: does the file exist, is the extension allowed, is it big enough, is the PDF readable. Pure read-only functions plus passive cloud-placeholder detection for OneDrive and Google Drive.
tracker/validators.py.notes: Never downloads a cloud-only placeholder — a stub must never be filed as if it were the document. A file that vanishes between listing and stat is reported pending_sync, never raised — a scheduled scan must not die on one replaced file.

tracker/content_check.py.role: Tier 3: extract text (pdfplumber / openpyxl / plain text, optional OCR) and test it against the row's keyword and date rules. Caches verdicts.
tracker/content_check.py.notes: The cache stores pass/fail only. Extracted client text is never persisted.

tracker/router.py.role: Decides which single manifest row a dropped file belongs to. Evidence order: required keywords, then any-keywords/period, then filename (text-less scans only).
tracker/router.py.notes: Extension alone never routes. A document matching one row's required keywords but failing its other rules is contested and blocks its own filing — misfiling a tax document is worse than not filing it. When nothing routes, the reason is the most useful one available: a document whose content fits a row that refused the file (size floor, type, unreadable PDF) is reported as 'looks like A01 (...)', and a file every row refused for the same reason carries that reason. The filename fallback also accepts the run-together spelling (W2 for W-2) as a whole token.

tracker/filer.py.role: Sorts the client's drop folder: moves each original into Shared/PBC/ untouched, copies a renamed working file into Prepared/... or 00 - Needs Review, and appends every move to _index.xlsx.
tracker/filer.py.notes: Content-hash de-duplication makes re-runs no-ops. Originals are moved byte for byte under their own names and never altered. Each drop is handled on its own: a drop that cannot be moved is left in place for the next run, a drop that fails after it was preserved is indexed as Needs Review with the error, and the index is written in a finally block so nothing moved into PBC/ is ever unrecorded. If Excel holds _index.xlsx, new rows wait in _index.pending.json and read_index() already sees them.

tracker/scanner.py.role: The orchestrator: walks Prepared/, runs the three validation tiers, resolves each row's status (override- and revert-aware), and writes the result back into the manifest.
tracker/scanner.py.notes: Holds a stale-aware per-engagement run lock, so two scheduled runs cannot overlap. Never touches Shared/ at all.

tracker/rollover.py.role: Builds a returning client's next-year request list from their prior engagement. Prior-year data always wins; the template may only fill blanks.
tracker/rollover.py.notes: Years shift as a set so relative periods stay right. Counts learn from what arrived and never shrink. Waived carries forward; Accepted does not. NOTE: rollover and api import each other - api imports rollover at module scope, rollover imports api only inside its __main__ block. That cycle is deliberate; do not "fix" it by hoisting the import.

tracker/reminder.py.role: Drafts the client chase email from a scanned manifest. Draft only — there is no SMTP anywhere in this module.
tracker/reminder.py.notes: Validation notes are translated into plain client instructions, never quoted. Rows we have not read yet, and rows with no request folder, are held back for a person instead of being asked for. Each draft carries a fingerprint of its own text so an edited draft is never overwritten. A Partial row whose shortfall is a file we have not read is held back too.

tracker/registry.py.role: Loads and validates engagements.yaml — the one file listing every engagement the scheduled run touches.
tracker/registry.py.notes: Fails loudly on an unknown key, a bad date or a duplicated path, because a typo that silently skipped a client would surface at a filing deadline. A missing folder is NOT rejected here; that is the runner's call, per engagement.

tracker/runner.py.role: The unattended pass: for every engagement in the registry, file -> scan -> (on Saturdays) draft. This is the whole scheduled task.
tracker/runner.py.notes: Owns the Saturday rule in is_draft_day(); the scheduler does not know about it. One engagement's failure never stops the others, and the run exits non-zero so the scheduler shows red. A drop the filer could not sort marks the engagement failed (exit non-zero) after the scan and draft still ran.

tracker/scheduling.py.role: Generates the Windows Task Scheduler XML or n8n workflow that runs tracker.runner unattended.
tracker/scheduling.py.notes: One daily task is enough because the runner decides the drafting day. Recognizes Windows drive-letter paths as absolute even when generating from Linux.

tracker/api.py.role: The JSON command layer the desktop app talks to: state, scaffold, sort, scan, create, rollover, templates, list, priors, reset. Also holds FORM_TEMPLATES (the per-form request checklists) and the demo sample-file builder.
tracker/api.py.notes: Every command prints one JSON object and returns an exit code — errors are JSON too, never a traceback. This is the only module the Electron app knows about. The create path validates identifiers and counts with the same sentences the manifest loader uses, and never leaves a half-built engagement folder behind.

tracker/__init__.py.role: Package docstring listing every component, and the re-exports of the manifest and scaffold APIs.

api_entry.py.role: PyInstaller entry point. Freezes tracker.api into tracker-api.exe for the portable Windows demo.
api_entry.py.notes: The only reason this exists is that PyInstaller needs a real script, not a -m module.

.github/workflows/ci.yml.role: CI: runs the test suite and `repo_map.py check` on every push to main and every pull request.
.github/workflows/ci.yml.notes: The map check is the point. docs/repo-map.md is what agents read instead of re-scanning, its freshness is guarded by test_the_committed_map_is_current, and this workflow is what makes that guard run without anyone remembering to. Both steps always report, so a stale map and a failing test surface in the same run.

CLAUDE.md.role: Agent entry point. Says to read the map instead of re-scanning, how to keep it current, and the standing rules that hold across every module.
CLAUDE.md.notes: Points at docs/repo-map.md as the first thing to read in a session.

docs/repo-map.curated.json.role: The hand-written half of this map: roles, notes, artifacts, cross-language hops and the standing rules. Merged on top of the derived facts and never overwritten by a rebuild.
docs/repo-map.curated.json.notes: Edit this, then run `python tools/repo_map.py update`. The generated docs/repo-map.json and docs/repo-map.md are NOT edited by hand.

tests/test_repo_map.py.role: Guards the map's trust contract: derived facts come from source, curated judgment survives regeneration, drift is detected, and the committed map matches the tree.
tests/test_repo_map.py.notes: test_the_committed_map_is_current fails the suite if someone changed code without running `repo_map.py update`.

conftest.py.role: Puts the repo root on sys.path so tests can `import tracker` without installing the package.

tools/repo_map.py.role: Builds and incrementally updates this map. Derives imports, exports, CLIs, test coverage and hashes from source; merges the curated layer on top.
tools/repo_map.py.notes: Standard library only. `update` re-parses only files whose SHA-256 changed, and a change to this file forces a full rebuild — new derivation rules must not leave edges typed by the old ones. Test edges are three-way on purpose: `tests` (the test file owning the module by name) is coverage, `exercises` (any other test importing it) is not, and a test importing another test is a plain `imports`.

app/main.js.role: Electron main process. Spawns the Python API (`python -m tracker.api`, or the frozen tracker-api.exe in the portable build) and relays its JSON to the renderer over IPC.
app/main.js.notes: This is the cross-language boundary: everything the UI can do is a tracker.api command.

app/preload.js.role: Context bridge exposing exactly two calls to the renderer: tracker.call(args, payload) and tracker.open(path). Nothing else crosses.

app/renderer/app.js.role: The desktop UI: the form-type wizard, the request list and the scan results. Talks only to window.tracker from the preload bridge.

demo/standalone/tax-document-tracker.htm.role: A single self-contained HTML file that ports the scanner's rules to the browser. Opens offline with nothing installed, for emailing to staff or demoing on a prospect's laptop.
demo/standalone/tax-document-tracker.htm.notes: A faithful port, not a shim: same statuses and same validation notes as the Python scanner. It has to be kept in step with tracker/scanner.py and tracker/validators.py by hand.

demo/demo_manifest.py.role: Hands-on walkthrough of the manifest layer, including the Excel-lock retry and sidecar behaviour you can watch live by holding the file open in Excel.

docs/ROADMAP.md.role: The build plan, the hard constraints and the decision log. Components 1-10, all built and tested.
docs/ROADMAP.md.notes: The decision log is the record of WHY: read it before changing behaviour that looks arbitrary.

README.md.role: What the system is, how to run each stage, and the two ways to demo it.

DEMO-SCRIPT.md.role: The script for walking someone through a demo.

requirements.txt.role: Runtime and dev dependencies; the optional OCR extras are documented here too.

artifact:_manifest.xlsx.role: The engagement's request list and its live status. Sits OUTSIDE the client's shared scope — the accountant's file, not theirs.

artifact:_index.xlsx.role: Every original the client sent: where it came from, where it went, and what it was renamed to. The audit trail.

artifact:_manifest.pending.json.role: Sidecar holding status updates that could not be written because Excel had the manifest locked. Merged into the next successful write.

artifact:_index.pending.json.role: Sidecar holding index rows for originals already moved into PBC/ that could not be written because Excel had _index.xlsx open. Read alongside the workbook and folded into the next successful write.

artifact:Shared/.role: The client's one drop folder — the only thing they see and the only thing they touch. Their originals end up in Shared/PBC/, still visible to them, untouched.

artifact:Prepared/.role: The firm-side working set: renamed copies sorted per request, plus 00 - Needs Review for anything that could not be identified. The client never sees this.

artifact:reminder-draft.txt.role: The drafted chase email, waiting for a person to read, edit and send. Carries a fingerprint so the weekly job can tell whether it has been edited.

artifact:engagements.yaml.role: The registry: every engagement the scheduled run should process. Gitignored — it names real clients and carries their share links.

rule:no-AI-on-client-documents.role: No generative AI ever reads a client financial document. Every routing and status decision comes from deterministic rules in the manifest.

rule:originals-are-never-altered.role: Originals are moved byte for byte under their own names into Shared/PBC/ and never renamed in place, edited or deleted. All work happens on copies.

rule:nothing-is-guessed.role: A document is filed only when exactly one request accepts it. Ambiguous, contested and unrecognized files go to 00 - Needs Review for a person.

rule:nothing-is-ever-sent.role: The system drafts client emails and stops. There is no SMTP, no mail client and no network call in the reminder or scheduling path; a person always sends.
